title: FACULTY AND COURSE MEMBERS OF 66TH NATIONAL DEFENCE COLLEGE COURSE CALL ON THE PRESIDENT
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The faculty and course members of the 66th National Defence College Course called on the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (October 13, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the security and technological landscapes are changing rapidly, bringing new and complex challenges. These developments call for greater preparedness, strategic foresight and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances. Fast decision-making mechanism is also becoming more important because the techniques of modern warfare have expanded into cyber security, space technology, and biotechnology apart from the traditional domains.
The President said that today, national security extends beyond military capabilities. It requires close cooperation between scientific institutions and the armed forces to translate innovation into practical solutions. Recent conflicts have highlighted the importance of cost-effective technologies that complement advanced defence systems and make the best use of available resources. She underlined the importance of government initiatives such as the Research, Development and Innovation Scheme, for strengthening the link between innovation and national security.
The President said that the use of Artificial Intelligence in various domains of science, national security and economic activities is increasing.
She said that decision making cannot be outsourced exclusively to this technology and emphasised the need for a balanced approach.
The President underlined that
economic resilience is an integral part of national security framework. She said that Indian economy has demonstrated its capabilities to absorb disruptions created by external factors. India has accomplished this without compromising the strategic freedom of action.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum
subtitle:
The vision I have come with is power to empower; Beyond the power to control, power to enable; Beyond the power to compete, power to collaborate; Beyond the power to succeed, power to help others succeed: PM

Our constant endeavour is to ensure that India's capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well: PM

India's progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities: PM

We do not grow at anyone's cost; We grow with the world and for the world: PM

In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability: PM

For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today addressed the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. Acknowledging Mr. Michael Bloomberg’s earlier remarks, the Prime Minister celebrated the forum's unprecedented debut in India. He praised the platform's ability to unite the world’s brightest minds to deliberate on key global themes, including the economy, technology, energy, and international affairs. "I congratulate Mr. Bloomberg and his entire team; you have chosen the right place at the right time,” remarked Shri Modi.
Addressing the summit's core focus on emerging global powers, the Prime Minister highlighted a monumental paradigm shift in the 21st century's third decade, where technology, data, knowledge, and innovation have become the ultimate metrics of power. He challenged the audience to reconsider the fundamental purpose of this power, questioning whether it should elevate a select few or actively democratize opportunities for millions, emphasizing a shift from controlling to enabling and from competing to collaborating. '“Moving beyond the power to succeed to the power to help others succeed, the vision with which I have come here today is Power to Empower,” asserted Shri Modi.
Grounding this philosophy in ancient cultural wisdom, the Prime Minister quoted traditional Sanskrit texts emphasizing that the true value of knowledge, wealth, and power is determined entirely by how ethically they are utilized. He stressed that understanding this profound purpose of power is absolutely essential for navigating today’s complex global dynamics. "Meaning, the true value of Power lies in its Purpose,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Translating these ancient ideals into modern administration, the Prime Minister stated that the concept of 'Power to Empower' is not a mere global sermon but a deeply ingrained cultural tradition actively applied to the nation’s governance and work culture. He announced his intention to illustrate this transformative philosophy using concrete examples of the nation's progress. "Therefore, I will take my point forward using examples from India itself,” noted Shri Modi.
Showcasing the vibrant dynamism of the 'Mother of Democracy', the Prime Minister proudly listed the nation's massive linguistic diversity, its 80,000 publications, and over a thousand television channels. He emphasized that in the modern social media era, the nation's half-a-billion YouTube and Instagram users engage in robust, open debates, proving that digital power is actively fueling democratic discourse. "In present times, what has played a major role in this is digital power,” observed Shri Modi.
Recounting the aggressive battle against digital exclusion, the Prime Minister noted that just over a decade ago, mere access to mobile phones and the internet was considered an elite privilege. He explained that since 2014, the government deliberately slashed data prices down to ensure that everyone from small-town students to village shopkeepers could instantly access knowledge and markets. "Meaning, Connectivity in India has not just connected people; it has also connected opportunities,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the extraordinary scale of financial inclusion, the Prime Minister invited international guests to witness a seamless digital payments ecosystem where a humble street vendor and a massive car showroom utilize the exact same technological platform. He framed this radical financial democratization as the ultimate proof of inclusive technology at work. "This is the strength of Inclusive Technology,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing the nation's commitment to international technological solidarity, the Prime Minister declared that domestic digital capabilities are continuously shared with the Global South and other partner countries to help them build their own Digital Public Infrastructure. He cited the open-source CoWIN platform, deployed during the pandemic, as a prime example of domestic innovation actively unlocking global possibilities. "Meaning, our capability should empower humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.
Championing the massive democratization of innovation, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's explosive startup growth, which skyrocketed from a few hundred in 2014 to over 2.5 lakh today. He proudly pointed out that nearly half of these startups originate from smaller cities and that over 45 percent feature female leadership, proving that the power to solve problems is reaching all segments of society. "Meaning, opportunities for Innovation are reaching more people,” noted Shri Modi.
Pivoting to the core philosophy of public administration, the Prime Minister stated that governmental authority must never aim to create systemic dependency, but must instead focus on rendering citizens entirely capable and empowered. He credited this exact empowerment-driven governance model for successfully lifting 25 crore people out of poverty over the last decade. "And India is walking on this very path,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the systemic eradication of corruption, the Prime Minister highlighted the deployment of the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer systems to deliver government assistance directly into citizens' bank accounts. "This has reduced corruption, increased the convenience of the country's citizens, and established a direct relationship between Government and Citizen,” observed Shri Modi.
Illustrating this empowerment philosophy on the global stage, the Prime Minister recalled the critical vaccine shortages during the COVID-19 pandemic and questioned whether life-saving manufacturing power should have been hoarded by a few nations. He expressed immense pride that the nation chose a humanitarian path by supplying vaccines to over 100 countries. "Our Manufacturing Capability became a medium of assistance for other countries as well,” asserted Shri Modi.
Presenting a unique example of inclusive foresight, the Prime Minister mentioned a recent domestic AI Impact summit that expanded the dialogue beyond human applications to actively discuss how artificial intelligence could benefit animal welfare. He used this anecdote to prove that an increasingly capable nation will continually generate broader benefits for the entire world. "The more capable India becomes, the more beneficial it will be for humanity, for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Calling for a balanced global order, the Prime Minister argued that while competition, innovation, and national strength are vital, they must be fundamentally paired with compassion and a commitment to solving global challenges like climate change, water governance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies. He insisted that the world desperately needs powers that actively create new, shared opportunities. "Power is not just the ability to move ahead; it is also the ability to empower others to move ahead,” asserted Shri Modi.
Demonstrating the nation's fierce commitment to climate action, the Prime Minister recalled the bold 2015 Paris Agreement pledge to achieve 40 percent installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030. He proudly announced that the nation surpassed this target in November 2021, nine years ahead of schedule, becoming the very first G20 country to do so. "This was not just about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a sign of India's changing Energy Journey,” noted Shri Modi.
Quantifying this massive green energy pivot, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's renewable energy capacity has skyrocketed from a mere 75 gigawatts in 2014 to approximately 300 gigawatts today. He highlighted this four-fold expansion as a monumental achievement in the country's sustainable development.
Explaining the grassroots economic benefits of this energy transition, the Prime Minister detailed how the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM schemes are actively empowering households and farmers to generate their own solar power and slash input costs. He noted that these initiatives have added over 30 gigawatts of capacity, reducing carbon emissions by over 30 million tonnes annually while simultaneously protecting nature and enriching citizens. "And it is also empowering people,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Contrasting the nation's cooperative ethos with global power struggles, the Prime Minister stated that amidst international races for dominance, the country is intentionally forging a distinct, stabilizing path. He noted that the current decade serves as an undeniable witness to this unique national temperament. "In this race for Power in the world, India is moving ahead with a different temperament,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing the cascading shocks defining the 21st century's third decade, the Prime Minister listed the rapid succession of global pandemics, regional wars, and severe supply chain disruptions affecting critical minerals, energy, and trade. He painted a stark picture of a world where one crisis barely recedes before another emerges. "The world searches for a way out of one crisis; by then, a new crisis emerges,” observed Shri Modi.
Condemning the weaponization of global interconnectedness, the Prime Minister lamented that essential elements like supply chains, energy, minerals, technology, and payment systems are being actively exploited as instruments of pressure and dominance. He warned that the integration achieved by decades of globalization is rapidly fracturing into dangerous geopolitical chokepoints. "The roots that globalization created in past decades, when and where they turned into chokepoints, we all are seeing this,” noted Shri Modi.
Addressing the resulting global crisis of confidence amidst rapid technological disruption and demographic challenges, the Prime Minister stated that the world is desperately searching for reliable partners who will maintain supply lines and honor commitments during crises. He positioned the nation as the ultimate dependable ally offering a radically different, cooperative approach to global relations. "And it is right here, India stands before you with a different temperament, a different thought,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Defining the nation's global operating model, the Prime Minister declared that the country's 21st-century progress is fundamentally defined by collaborative, inclusive advancement. He cited the nation's role as the provider of one-fifth of the world's generic medicines, a pioneer of digital identity models, and a trusted talent hub hosting over 2,000 Global Capability Centres servicing the globe. "India's progress is the story of moving forward by collaborating with everyone, by taking everyone along,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reiterating the nation's role as a stabilizing global force, the Prime Minister emphasized that whenever the world requires a steady pillar, the country responsibly extends its hand to support the international community. He outlined a fundamental philosophy of equitable advancement on the global stage. “We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world, and for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Drawing upon profound historical legacy, the Prime Minister pointed out that the nation historically gifted the concept of 'Zero' to humanity without ever demanding royalties, and continues to operate with that exact same selfless spirit today. He contrasted this with historical global organizations that operated strictly on self-interest. "And even today India is working with this same spirit,” noted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the nation's track record of building inclusive global platforms, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Big Cat Alliance, the Global Biofuel Alliance, IMEC, and Mission LiFE. He stressed that these platforms were intentionally designed to generate universal benefits for all forms of life rather than serving narrow geopolitical interests. "Meaning those which benefit everyone, which benefit every life, India has taken such initiatives,” asserted Shri Modi.
Summarizing the overarching philosophical framework driving the nation's foreign policy, the Prime Minister invoked the visions of 'One Sun, One World, One Grid', 'One Earth, One Family, One Future', and 'One Earth, One Health'. He emphasized that the country exclusively utilizes its power to connect, unite, and elevate others. "And even in this, the use of Power is only to Empower others,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Showcasing the nation's macroeconomic resilience amidst global uncertainty, the Prime Minister proudly cited a 7.8 percent growth rate for the April-June quarter, a current account deficit slashed to a mere 0.61 percent, and foreign exchange reserves exceeding 700 billion dollars. He declared that the domestic banking system is currently enjoying its strongest position in decades. "In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability,” asserted Shri Modi.
Attributing recent sovereign rating upgrades to this immense structural strength, the Prime Minister highlighted the relentless execution of systemic reforms, including the implementation of GST to create a unified national market, the drafting of Insolvency Laws, the consolidation of 29 labor codes into four, and the decriminalization of hundreds of minor business offenses. He assured global investors that this unstoppable momentum is a deliberate, proactive choice driving the nation forward. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by invoking the ancient Vedic mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the global community to walk, speak, and understand one another together to multiply collective strength and solve major global challenges. He expressed profound confidence that the Bloomberg New Economy Forum would serve as a massive platform to propagate this exact spirit of creating shared global opportunities.

title: English rendering of PM’s address at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 11:08AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Namaskar!
Excellencies, delegates from around the world, leaders from business and industry, policymakers, and my friends.
A very warm welcome to all of you to India. A short while ago, Mr. Bloomberg shared his thoughts here. Reflecting on his 30-year journey, he mentioned that I am his friend. He is senior to me in age and is a highly successful person in his professional field. He is not only successful but also deeply committed. The affection he has for India is something I have experienced very closely, and therefore, on a personal level, I have always respected and admired him. Even today, his affection for India and his sentiments towards India on global platforms have consistently been a source of very positive energy. For that, sir, I express my heartfelt gratitude. Every year, this Forum brings together some of the finest minds in the world. Discussions here take place on the economy, technology, energy, and global affairs. And this time, for the very first time, the event is being held in India. I warmly congratulate Mr. Bloomberg and his entire team for this decision. You have chosen the right place at the right time.
Friends,
This year's Bloomberg Economic Forum is focused on the new powers emerging around the world. Every era has had its own sources of power and its own definition of power. But in the 21st century, especially in this third decade, a major transformation is taking place. Today, Technology is Power, Data is Power, Knowledge is Power, Innovation is Power.
But friends,
The real question is not who possesses power. Rather, the question is how that power is being used. Will technology advance only a few people? Or will it create new opportunities for millions? Will knowledge remain the strength of only a select few? Or will it enhance everyone's capabilities? It is from here that a new idea emerges. And that idea is: Power to Empower. Power to Empower. Beyond Power to Control lies Power to Enable. Beyond Power to Compete lies Power to Collaborate. Beyond Power to Succeed lies Power to Help Others Succeed. And therefore, the vision with which I have come here today is: Power to Empower.
Friends,
This idea is not new to India. In our tradition, it is said: "Vidya Vivadaya Dhanam Madaya, Shaktih Paresham Paripidanaya; Khalasya Sadhoh Viparitam Etat, Jnanaya Danaya Cha Rakshanaya." Its essence is that whoever possesses knowledge, wealth, or power, what matters is how they use it. In other words, the true value of power lies in its purpose. And it is very important to understand this philosophy in today's world.
Friends,
This human spirit of Power to Empower is not merely a lesson meant to be preached to others. It is something that our traditions have taught us over thousands of years. And in India, we have demonstrated this by incorporating it into our governance and our work culture. Therefore, I will continue my remarks through examples from India itself.
Friends,
As all of you know, India is the Mother of Democracy. India has more than one hundred languages, nearly eighty thousand registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels. And not only that, in this age of social media, India has more than five hundred million YouTube users and more than five hundred million Instagram users. In our country, people openly debate different issues, and citizens discuss diverse viewpoints. In the present era, one factor that has played a major role in enabling this is digital power.
Friends,
Until about twelve or thirteen years ago, there was a time in India when access to mobile phones and the internet itself was a form of power. Whoever had access also had information, knowledge, and opportunities. After 2014, when a new government came to power in India and we were given the opportunity to serve, India placed great emphasis on making mobile data affordable. As a result, today a student in a small town can access digital learning. A small shopkeeper in a village can reach new customers. A young person can enroll in online courses. In other words, connectivity in India has not merely connected people; it has connected opportunities as well. This, indeed, is Power to Empower.
Friends,
To those guests who have come from abroad, I would encourage you to experience India's digital payments ecosystem. In our country, a street vendor and a large car showroom may operate at completely different scales, but both use the same digital payments ecosystem. This is the strength of inclusive technology.
Friends,
Whatever capabilities India possesses, we do not believe in keeping them confined within our own borders. We continuously share them with the Global South and with our partner countries. We are sharing our experience in Digital Public Infrastructure with other nations so that they can develop digital systems according to their own needs. During the COVID period, we also developed the CoWIN platform, which was open source. In other words, our constant effort has been to ensure that India's capabilities open new doors of possibility for other countries as well. In other words, our strength should empower humanity.
Friends,
The power of innovation works in the same way. Transforming an idea into a product, and turning a problem into a solution, is in itself a tremendous capability. But when such opportunities reach a larger number of people in society, the balance of power becomes more equitable and its impact multiplies many times over. India's startup journey is an example of this transformation. Before 2014, India had only a few hundred startups. Today, the country has more than 250,000 startups. Nearly half of these startups come from small cities and towns. More than forty-five percent of startups have at least one woman Director or Partner. In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, new talent is emerging, and new solutions are being created.
Friends,
This focus on the purpose of power is equally important in governance. The government possesses authority, but its purpose should not be to make citizens dependent on the system. Rather, its objective should be to ensure that citizens become capable and empowered. India is moving along this very path. Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty over the past decade, a number greater than the population of many countries in the world.
Friends,
You may also have heard about the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer. By using technology, we have created a system through which government assistance reaches beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts. This has reduced corruption, increased convenience for citizens, and established a direct pathway between the government and the people.
Friends,
This same philosophy of Power to Empower is visible in India's global engagement. During the COVID pandemic, vaccine manufacturing capacity became extremely important. The question at that time was whether the benefits of this capability would remain limited to only a few countries, or whether vaccines would also reach those nations and people who lacked such facilities and capabilities. India chose the path of empowering humanity. We supplied vaccines to more than one hundred countries. Our manufacturing capability became a source of assistance for other nations as well. Let me give you another interesting example. A few months ago, India hosted the AI Impact Summit, and Mr. Bloomberg has just spoken very highly of that summit. There, we discussed not only the use of AI for humanity, but also how animals could benefit from AI. Nandan, who is seated here, can later share much more information about how this was done. In other words, the more capable and stronger India becomes, the more beneficial it will be for humanity and for the world.
Friends,
Power is not just the ability to move ahead. It is also the ability to empower others to move ahead. India believes that competition is important, but compassion is equally important. Innovation is essential, but its benefits must also be widely shared. National strength is necessary, but we must also contribute solutions to global challenges. Whether it is climate change, water governance, public health, or the responsible use of emerging technologies, the world needs capabilities that provide solutions and create new opportunities.
Friends,
Let me give you another example. Under the Paris Agreement, India made a major commitment to address climate change. In 2015, we set ourselves the target of achieving 40 percent of our installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030. India achieved this milestone in November 2021 itself, nine years ahead of schedule. India became the first G20 nation to do so. This was not merely about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a reflection of India's evolving energy journey.
Friends,
In 2014, India's renewable energy capacity stood at about 75 gigawatts. Today, it has reached approximately 300 gigawatts. In other words, we have added nearly four times more capacity.
Friends,
This energy transition underway in India is also creating new opportunities. Today, we have schemes such as PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM. One scheme is connecting households to solar power, while the other is enabling farmers to generate solar energy and reduce their input costs through its use. Through these two schemes, India has achieved more than 30 gigawatts of solar capacity. It is estimated that they will reduce carbon emissions by more than 30 million tonnes annually. In other words, solar power is not only becoming a means of protecting nature, but also a means of empowering people.
Friends,
In this global race for power, India is moving forward with a different mindset. And this decade itself bears witness to that.
Friends,
This decade of the twenty-first century has brought unprecedented global challenges. If we look back at the last six years, we witnessed a global pandemic. Then wars broke out in different regions. As if that were not enough, disruptions emerged in trade, critical minerals, and energy supplies. The world begins to find a way out of one crisis when another crisis appears. Things that once connected the world are now being turned into weapons. Supply chains, energy, minerals, payment systems, and technology are increasingly becoming instruments of pressure and dominance. The routes created by globalization over past decades have, in many cases, become chokepoints. Amid all this, Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way every sector functions. At the same time, many countries are facing rapidly growing challenges related to ageing populations. In such circumstances, the world is confronted with a fundamental question: trust. Trust that supplies will continue during times of need. Trust that promises made will also be fulfilled. Trust that a partner country will stand by you during moments of crisis. And it is here that India stands before you with a different outlook and a different way of thinking.
Friends,
India's progress in the twenty-first century is a story of advancing together with everyone and carrying everyone along. When the world needs affordable medicines, one out of every five generic medicines comes from India. When solutions for digital identity and payments are required, the world looks to models developed in India. When the world needs talent, it places its trust in India's skilled youth. Today, India is home to more than 2,000 Global Capability Centres that are providing services to companies across the world.
Friends,
It is clear that whenever the world needs a steady pillar, India extends its hand in support, recognizing its responsibility. We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world, and for the world.
And friends,
India does not seek credit for what it does. The world proudly says that India gave Zero to the world. This Zero benefited all of humanity. Yet India never asked for royalties in return. Even today, India works with the same spirit. The ideas we offer for addressing contemporary challenges also reflect this outlook. Throughout history, many global organizations have been created, each serving its own interests. But consider the kind of global platforms India has created. Consider the institutions we have established and compare them with what has emerged elsewhere in the world. What have we contributed? The International Solar Alliance. What have we contributed? The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. What have we contributed? The Big Cat Alliance, the Global Biofuel Alliance, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), and Mission LiFE, Lifestyle for Environment. These are initiatives that benefit everyone and contribute to the well-being of all life.
Friends,
The ideas that India has brought forward are before you. The vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid. The belief in One Earth, One Family, One Future. The vision of One Earth, One Health. In other words, India places emphasis on connecting and coming together. And even in this, power is used to empower others.
Friends,
In a world filled with uncertainty, India offers the assurance of reliability and stability. In the April-June quarter of this year, India's growth rate stood at 7.8 percent. And this growth rests on a strong foundation. Twelve to thirteen years ago, India's current account deficit was more than four percent of GDP. Last year, it declined to approximately half a percent, standing at 0.61 percent. Today, our foreign exchange reserves exceed 700 billion dollars. Our banking system is in its strongest position in many decades.
Friends,
It is because of this strength that India's sovereign ratings are being upgraded. Today, India's confidence is at an unprecedented high. We are pursuing reforms with a clear policy direction. Through GST, we transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market. We enacted the Insolvency Law. Twenty-nine labour laws have now been consolidated into four simple labour codes. Hundreds of minor business-related offences have been decriminalized. And we have not stopped there. India's reform express continues to move ahead at high speed. For us, reforms are not a compulsion. Reforms are our conviction.
Friends,
Thousands of years ago, our Vedas gave us a mantra: "Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manamsi Janatam. Let us repeat that mantra today: Let us walk together. Let us speak together. Let us strive to understand one another. Because when we walk together, our strength grows. Through dialogue, our understanding deepens. And by understanding one another, we can jointly solve great challenges. This is the essence of Power to Empower. It means not limiting our power solely to our own progress, but using it to create new opportunities for others as well. content:
Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) on “Management of Dermatological Disorders for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy”, with the inclusion of Yoga have been issued by the Ministry of Ayush. Prepared by the Ayush Vertical of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the document is intended to bring more uniformity, quality assurance and evidence-informed practice to clinical care across the Ayush systems.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, underlined that the guidelines would deepen the integration of Ayush systems with the national healthcare framework. “These guidelines bring together system-specific clinical approaches with contemporary scientific evidence to support safe, effective and holistic care for common dermatological conditions. By promoting standardised and evidence-informed clinical practice, they will contribute to improving patient care and strengthening the role of Ayush systems in public health,” the Minister said.
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, noted that the guidelines would help build standardisation and evidence-based clinical practice across the Ayush systems. “The Standard Treatment Guidelines for Dermatological Disorders are an important step towards strengthening standardisation, quality and evidence-based practice across the Ayush systems. Developed through expert consultations and evaluation of contemporary scientific evidence, these guidelines provide practical recommendations for prevention, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up while preserving the fundamental principles of each Ayush system. They will promote greater uniformity in clinical practice and support rational decision-making in patient care,” he said.
Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services, pointed to the value of multidisciplinary collaboration in improving dermatological care. “The Standard Treatment Guidelines on Dermatological Disorders are an important step towards promoting quality assurance, uniformity and evidence-based healthcare delivery across the Ayush systems. By fostering multidisciplinary collaboration, these guidelines will support Ayush practitioners in delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care,” he said.
The guidelines were made public on the occasion of the 11th Ayurveda Day. They represent a significant move towards a standardised approach to managing skin disorders through the Ayush systems. For each system, they set out specific recommendations on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, follow-up and rehabilitation for common dermatological conditions such as psoriasis, dermatitis, vitiligo, urticaria and dermatophytosis.
Interdisciplinary development
The preparation of the guidelines was a comprehensive, interdisciplinary effort. It drew on the technical expertise of the Ayush Research Councils, senior academic specialists in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy, Yoga experts, and specialists in modern medicine. The process comprised expert consultations, a review of classical texts, an assessment of current scientific evidence and consensus-based deliberations, all while retaining the core principles of each Ayush system.
Validation in real-world settings
A notable feature of the exercise was the field-level validation of the protocols, carried out to check how well they work in actual clinical settings. The Ayush Vertical partnered with the Directorate of Ayush, Government of NCT of Delhi, to test the protocols with Medical Officers working in primary and secondary healthcare. The feedback these officers gave on the operational usability of the guidelines was built into the final documents, improving their clinical relevance and practical value.
Expected benefits
The guidelines are expected to aid rational clinical decision-making, capacity building, education and further research. They will also serve as valuable reference documents for Ayush practitioners, clinicians, academicians, researchers and policymakers. The initiative further reflects the Government’s sustained emphasis on standardisation, quality assurance and the evidence-based integration of Ayush systems into healthcare delivery.

title: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav conduct joint review of stubble management
subtitle:
“Stubble is not a problem, but a solution for enhancing farmers’ income and improving soil health”: High-level inter-ministerial meeting held at Krishi Bhawan

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan sends a clear message to states: “Take action on a war footing to prevent stubble burning; very little time remains”

“We must protect the soil and ensure farmers’ prosperity”: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Machines must operate in fields, not merely exist on paper: Repair old machines and ensure their availability to small farmers at subsidised rates”: Shri Shivraj Singh

“The Central Government is extending all possible financial assistance to states; Punjab must submit its Utilisation Certificate (UC) promptly to enable the next instalment to be released”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

“Collectors must take charge in the field and work through micro-planning: Prepare a roadmap to convert stubble into electricity, bio-CNG and manure instead of smoke”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A high-level inter-ministerial review meeting was held today at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi, to implement crop residue (stubble) management in mission mode during the ongoing paddy harvesting season. The meeting was co-chaired by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, and Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, the agriculture ministers of key states, including Delhi-NCR, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, Union Secretary for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Narendra Bhushan, and other senior officials from the Central and state governments were present at the meeting.
During the meeting, both Union Ministers made it clear that very little time remained between the completion of crop harvesting and the sowing of rabi crops. Therefore, the administrative machinery must move beyond files and take action directly on the ground on a war footing. They issued firm directions for district-level collectors to convene meetings promptly, strengthen monitoring and ensure that practical solutions were implemented without delay. The emphasis was on swift coordination and effective action at the field level to prevent stubble burning during the critical period.
“Stubble is not a problem, but a means of improving farmers’ income and soil health”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Addressing the meeting, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that paddy harvesting was underway and farmers were eager to prepare their fields for the next crop. In such circumstances, merely telling farmers not to burn stubble would not be enough. They must be provided with alternatives that are easy to use, readily accessible and affordable. Stubble burning not only causes air pollution but also destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns away essential nutrients, turning them into ash. It is therefore necessary to protect Mother Earth and preserve soil health. When crop residue is incorporated into the soil, it can be converted into organic manure; when removed from the field, it can serve as a source of additional income for farmers through its use in bio-CNG, bio-ethanol, electricity generation and animal fodder.
He further stated that the objective was not merely to prevent stubble fires but to develop a robust system in which farmers would have no need to burn crop residue in the first place. The aim should be to create practical and economically viable arrangements for managing stubble while enabling farmers to benefit from opportunities such as carbon credits through environmentally sustainable agricultural practices. Such an approach would protect the environment while also strengthening farmers’ livelihoods and improving the long-term sustainability of agriculture.
Concern over rising incidents in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan; directions issued for action on a war footing
Commenting on the analysis of the data presented during the meeting, Shri Shivraj Chouhan said it was encouraging that, between September 15 and October 12, stubble-burning incidents had declined significantly compared with the corresponding period last year. Haryana recorded a reduction of 53.3 per cent, while Uttar Pradesh registered a decline of approximately 32 per cent. Punjab had also recorded some reduction. However, expressing concern over the increase in stubble-burning incidents in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, the Union Agriculture Minister directed both states to identify the affected districts and villages and immediately implement special action plans to address the situation. He emphasised that a substantial portion of harvesting was still pending. Therefore, even states that had achieved a reduction in incidents must not become complacent and should maintain complete vigilance throughout the remaining harvesting period.
Ensure 100 per cent utilisation of machines; prevent older machines from remaining out of operation
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan placed particular emphasis on ensuring that crop residue management machinery remained operational and was put to effective use. He stated that the Central Government had so far provided states with more than 3.54 lakh crop residue management machines, including 26,109 new machines during the current financial year, 2026–27. He directed the authorities to ensure that, alongside the distribution of new machines, older machines that had become non-functional were repaired immediately and brought back into operation. Failure to do so could create an unnecessary shortage of equipment despite the machinery already available. He also stressed the need to activate Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) and ensure that small and marginal farmers could access the required machinery at affordable, subsidised rates. The focus must be on making the equipment genuinely available to farmers when they need it, rather than allowing it to remain unused.
Substantial financial assistance from the Centre; Punjab urged to submit Utilisation Certificate promptly
Regarding the availability of funds, the meeting was informed that the Central Government had released a substantial amount of ₹4,266.47 crore to states under the Crop Residue Management (CRM) scheme between 2018–19 and 2025–26. This included ₹2,056.50 crore for Punjab, ₹1,171.71 crore for Haryana, ₹868.67 crore for Uttar Pradesh and ₹59 crore for Madhya Pradesh. For the current financial year, 2026–27, an allocation of ₹592.57 crore had also been earmarked, of which ₹430.87 crore had already been released. However, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan expressed concern over the slow utilisation of the allocated funds. He stressed that farmers must receive the necessary resources and equipment in time for them to manage crop residue effectively. In particular, the Punjab Government was urged to submit the Utilisation Certificate (UC) for the funds released earlier to the Centre without delay. This would enable the next instalment under the scheme to be released promptly and without any disruption, ensuring the continued availability of financial support for crop residue management measures.
Use stubble as fodder in drought-affected areas; establish direct links between farmers and industries
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan directed that, in areas facing drought-like conditions, stubble should be collected and stored safely for use as animal fodder and subsequently supplied to livestock. He also called for farmers to be connected directly with supply chains serving thermal power plants for the co-firing of stubble pellets, compressed biogas (CBG) facilities and second-generation (2G) bio-ethanol plants. Such linkages would help create additional avenues for the productive utilisation of crop residue and provide farmers with opportunities to earn additional income. He asked state governments to ensure that approved supply projects were implemented on the ground without delay. He also stressed the need to encourage improved, short-duration paddy varieties, such as Pusa 2090 and PR126, in place of longer-duration varieties such as Pusa-44. Shorter-duration varieties would allow farmers to harvest their crops earlier and provide sufficient time to clear their fields before the next sowing season.
Assurance of all possible assistance to states
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the primary responsibility for implementation at the grassroots level rested with state governments. However, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Central Government stood firmly alongside states and farmers, extending all possible technical, administrative and financial support at every stage. He called upon all participating ministries, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and district administrations to treat stubble management as a shared national commitment and work collectively towards its effective implementation. He emphasised that coordinated efforts by the Centre, state governments and local administrations were essential to ensure that practical solutions reached farmers in time. The ultimate objective was to keep agricultural fields free from pollution, protect soil health, improve farmers’ livelihoods and contribute to the prosperity of the farming community.
“Strict monitoring of the satellite observation gap after 3 PM directed”: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav stressed the need to intensify ground-level monitoring and enforcement measures to prevent stubble-burning incidents. He called for special vigilance in key districts of Punjab, including Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Amritsar, Patiala and Gurdaspur, as well as in Haryana districts such as Kaithal, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Ambala and Fatehabad. The objective was to assess crop-harvesting patterns in these areas and anticipate the likelihood of stubble-burning incidents so that preventive measures could be undertaken in advance. He emphasised the importance of identifying vulnerable areas and strengthening local monitoring arrangements during the ongoing harvesting season.
Shri Yadav highlighted the need to integrate data relating to stubble burning with the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to improve the effectiveness of monitoring. He said it was important to forecast the likely timing of harvesting in the coming days and closely monitor meteorological conditions that could affect air pollution levels in the National Capital Region (NCR). Such information would help authorities assess the evolving situation and take the necessary action in a timely manner. He also called for effective evaluation of the impact of interventions and the identification of corrective measures to address emerging challenges. Continuous assessment of the measures being implemented would be essential to strengthen the response and improve the effectiveness of efforts to prevent crop residue burning.
Emphasising that monitoring must not depend solely on satellite data, Shri Yadav said district collectors should undertake ground-level assessments and strengthen enforcement measures to make efforts to prevent crop residue burning more effective. He underlined the need for strict surveillance through ground patrols and flying squads during the gap in satellite monitoring after 3 PM, when no satellite pass is available. This period requires particular attention to ensure that incidents of stubble burning do not go undetected. He stressed that a combination of satellite-based monitoring, field inspections and effective enforcement would help authorities respond more promptly and prevent the burning of crop residue during the critical harvesting period.

title: Improved Soybean Varieties NRC 268 and NRC 270 Show Promising Signs of Yielding 20 Quintals per Hectare Despite Adverse Weather Conditions
subtitle:
Compilation of yield data to help assess future productivity gains: Dr. M. L. Jat

ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, Organises Soybean Harvest Day; Scientific Analysis of Yield Data to Assess Potential for Productivity Enhancement
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), organised a Soybean Harvest Day on 9 October 2026. On this occasion, the yield potential of the improved soybean
Varieties
NRC 268 and NRC 270, developed by the Institute, was assessed. Preliminary data obtained after harvesting one acre each under the two varieties indicate encouraging yields of approximately 20 quintals per hectare. This assessment is important for understanding the performance of improved varieties under adverse weather conditions and evaluating the potential for enhancing soybean productivity in the country. At present, the average soybean productivity in India is approximately 10–11 quintals per hectare.
Research and trials conducted across the country by ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute and under the All India Coordinated Research Project on Soybean indicate that yields of 15–20 quintals per hectare can be achieved by adopting improved varieties and appropriate production technologies. Under favourable conditions, yields may potentially reach approximately 22–25 quintals per hectare.
Appreciating these preliminary findings, Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), said that improved varieties and scientific production technologies play a significant role in enhancing soybean productivity in the country. He stated that the indications of yields of approximately 20 quintals per hectare from NRC 200 68 and NRC 200 70, despite adverse weather conditions this year, were highly encouraging. He further emphasised that the scientific analysis of these data would help guide future research strategies aimed at increasing soybean productivity.
The Director of ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, stated that the significance of the data collected during Soybean Harvest Day extends beyond assessing the yield of a single year. Systematic collection and analysis of data over several years will help understand changes in productivity across different regions, varieties and production conditions. This will provide a scientific basis for assessing annual improvements in productivity and estimating the potential for future yield enhancement. Long-term data will also be useful in evaluating the effectiveness of research and technology dissemination efforts.
The Institute regularly organises such events to assess the actual yield potential of different soybean varieties, understand the impact of improved technologies, and disseminate information on high-yielding varieties and scientific production practices to farmers. This initiative will help strengthen coordination among soybean research, agricultural extension services and the dissemination of scientific knowledge to farmers.
The primary objective of the Soybean Harvest Day was to assess the yield potential of improved varieties and establish a scientific basis for enhancing productivity through the systematic collection of yield data. The data obtained from the harvest will be analysed further to develop a better understanding of varietal performance and the influence of different production conditions.

title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completes five years of transforming India’s infrastructure landscape
subtitle:
PM GatiShakti integrates more than 1,800 data layers covering 58 Central Ministries/Departments and all 36 States/UTs

Network Planning Group evaluates more than 400 infrastructure projects worth ₹20.23 Lakh Crore

PM GatiShakti expands to district-level and social-sector planning; Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority to strengthen multimodal connectivity
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in October 2021, is completing five years, marking significant progress in integrated infrastructure planning and development in the country.
The PM GatiShakti geospatial digital platform has been developed indigenously under Atmanirbhar Bharat by the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N). With the vision of bringing synergy across Ministries/Departments and States/Union Territories, PM GatiShakti has established a Whole-of-Government approach to infrastructure planning by integrating geospatial data, facilitating coordinated decision-making and strengthening multimodal, intermodal and last-mile connectivity. Over the last five years, the initiative has evolved from an integrated digital planning platform into a comprehensive geospatial planning ecosystem supporting infrastructure, economic and social-sector development.
The PM GatiShakti digital platform integrated more than 1,800 data layers, covering 58 Central Ministries/Departments and all 36 States/Union Territories. The platform has also facilitated the development and integration of more than 65 software modules/tools and over 100 mobile and web applications, strengthening data-driven infrastructure planning across the country.
The Network Planning Group (NPG) evaluated over 400 infrastructure projects worth approximately ₹20.23 lakh crore based on PM GatiShakti principles. The evaluation framework emphasises integrated planning and development of multimodal infrastructure, last-mile connectivity to economic and social nodes, intermodal connectivity, improved logistics efficiency and synchronised implementation of projects. NPG institutionalised the Whole-of-Government approach.
PM GatiShakti expanded beyond conventional infrastructure planning to support social-sector development and area-based planning. The initiative progressively extended to districts, supporting integrated planning for local socio-economic development, including roads, schools, healthcare facilities, water pipelines and other essential services at the district level.
The PM GatiShakti Public platform, through the Unified Geospatial Interface (UGI), was launched in September 2025, extending selected data-analytics capabilities to private entities and the general public. The Knowledge Management System (KMS), Decentralized Data Uploading and Management System (DUMS) and PMGS-NMP Dashboard have further strengthened knowledge sharing, data governance, decentralised data management and infrastructure monitoring.
Since its launch in 2021–22, PM GatiShakti progressed through successive phases of foundation, expansion, deepening, digitalisation and accessibility. During 2022–23, eight key infrastructure Ministries were onboarded and 71 projects were evaluated. In 2023–24, social-sector integration was undertaken, with 1,463 data layers and all 36 States/Union Territories onboarded.
During 2024–25, economic-sector integration was undertaken, the District Master Plan was launched and 121 projects were evaluated. In 2025–26, the PM GatiShakti Public platform/UGI, KMS, DUMS and Dashboard were launched, with 352 projects evaluated by February 2026.
In 2026, 421 projects worth ₹20.23 lakh crore had been evaluated, alongside the integration of approximately 1,800 data layers, more than 65 tools and over 100 applications. The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority was also approved by the Union Cabinet.
Over the last five years, PM GatiShakti has progressed from establishing an integrated national planning framework to developing a wider geospatial ecosystem for infrastructure and regional development. Through the integration of data, institutional coordination, project appraisal, digital tools and district-level planning, the initiative continues to support a more integrated approach to infrastructure development.
To leverage the full potential of PM GatiShakti for integrated long-term transport planning, the Government has decided to set up the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment within the broad domains of transportation and logistics. Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in strengthening multimodal infrastructure connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness.

The speakers with diverse expertise will enable a substantive dialogue on semiconductor fabrication, chip design, AI computing, indigenous semiconductor platforms, research and development, and strategic and defence applications. The session is expected to foster stronger collaboration among industry, academia and strategic stakeholders, identify emerging technological opportunities and contribute to the development of a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, with emphasis on indigenous capabilities for critical and next-generation applications.

Dr Das added that strengthening domestic capabilities is critical to protecting the national economy from global supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical volatility and international technology export controls. He underlined India's aim to emerge as a global semiconductor powerhouse, advancing strategic autonomy and high-value exports across the microelectronics value chain.
Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Technology Management) Dr Anupam Sharma highlighted the critical role of semiconductors in modern warfare, stating that these technologies are integral to virtually every aspect of military operations. He added that business in the semiconductor-related segment is expected to rise to 200 billion dollars by 2035.

Northeast Economy Growing at 9–11% Annually, ₹40,000 Crore in Investments Grounded Across Eight States

Banking Touchpoints Cover 99.93% of Villages, 131 New Bank Branches and 126 ATMs Added

content:
Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today inaugurated the North East Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 at Mizoram University in Aizawl. The conclave focused on expanding banking access, strengthening financial inclusion and accelerating economic growth across the Northeast.
Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma, State Minister Prof. Lalnilawma, MDoNER Secretary Srinivas Katikithala, Chief Secretary Khilli Ram Meena and NEC Secretary Satinder Kumar Bhalla attended the event. Representatives from the RBI, SBI, Punjab National Bank, Central Bank of India, UCO Bank, Bank of Baroda, Indian Overseas Bank, Indian Bank, India Post Payments Bank, Canara Bank, Punjab & Sind Bank and IDBI Bank participated. Development institutions, including NABARD, SIDBI, DFS, NEDFi, NERAMAC and NECBDC, were also represented.
Addressing the North East Bankers’ Conclave, Shri Scindia urged banks to focus on three priorities: expanding physical banking infrastructure, improving credit access through state-wise Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio targets, and supporting MSMEs and infrastructure development.
Describing the Northeast as one of the most promising banking markets in India and globally, Union minister Scindia highlighted the region’s annual economic growth of 9–11%. Expressing his personal connection with the Northeast, he urged bankers to explore its growing opportunities and ensure that the economic value generated in the region remains within the region.
Greater Credit Flow to Drive Economic Growth
Highlighting the need to convert financial inclusion into economic inclusion, Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said only ₹47 is extended as credit for every ₹100 deposited in banks across the Northeast.
He urged banks to expand credit access for entrepreneurs, farmers, women and MSMEs, emphasising that the Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio should reflect “Credit for Development” in the Northeast.
The Minister also stressed the need for a Northeast-specific credit-risk framework. He noted that community-based landownership in the region requires flexible collateral rules to improve access to loans.
Banking Network Expands Across Northeast
Reviewing progress since the first North East Bankers’ Conclave, shri Scindia said approximately 73% progress had been achieved over five years against the banking targets set at the inaugural conclave.
Key achievements include :-
131 new bank branches and 126 ATMs added.
247 new India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) centres established.
6,674 bank branches and 5,823 ATMs operating across the region.
Banking touchpoints covering approximately 99.93% of villages.
2,500 additional IPPB access points planned.
Of approximately 9,000 villages identified for improved banking and postal coverage, 6,905 have been covered. The minimum population requirement for opening a physical bank branch has also been reduced from 3,000 to 2,000.
Highlighting the Northeast’s growing adoption of digital banking, Shri Scindia noted that UPI accounts for 90.2% of all non-branch transactions across the region.
₹40,000 Crore Investments Grounded in Northeast
Union Minister Scindia said approximately ₹40,000 crore in investments have been grounded across the eight northeastern states following the Rising North East Investors Summit in May 2025.
He highlighted major infrastructure improvements, including the expansion of the region's airport network from 9 to 17 airports.
He also cited the Bairabi railway line in Mizoram, which has carried approximately 15 lakh passengers through 1,100 trips.
The Minister said that the Northeast receives more than one lakh crore annually through the allocation of 10% of Gross Budgetary Support, monitored by MDoNER. He also highlighted approximately ₹6 lakh crore in fiscal devolution to the eight states.
Northeast Offers Strong Demographic Advantage
Highlighting the region’s demographic and economic potential, Shri Scindia noted that the Northeast has a population of approximately 5 crore. He underscored the importance of harnessing the region’s young population through greater opportunities in education, skill development, entrepreneurship and employment. He said that the average literacy rate across the eight states stands at 93%, while Mizoram has achieved 100% literacy.
Emphasising the region’s natural wealth and economic potential, Scindia said, “The Northeast has a demographic and educational bulge, an array of natural resources and extraordinary natural beauty. When you land at Lengpui, it feels as though you have landed in a forest. Mother Nature has gifted this region something truly exclusive.”
Highlighting the region’s economic growth, he said, “You are not entering an unexplored economic area. The world is growing. Guess what the annual growth rate of the Northeast is ?
It is 9-11% every single year.” He urged banks to play a key role in sustaining this growth.
Reflecting on his engagement with the region, Shri Scindia said, “I have been the Minister of DoNER for about 32 months, and this is my 35th visit to the Northeast. From its caves and rivers to its living root bridges, and from its entrepreneurs to the capabilities of its governments at the village level, I have witnessed the immense potential of this region.”
State-Wise Banking Roadmap
Union minister Scindia outlined four priorities for the Department of Financial Services (DFS): preparing a plan for 70 bank branches, Business Correspondents and IPPB points; strengthening commercial-bank presence; developing a Northeast-specific credit-risk framework; and preparing an action plan for the region's financial system.
He said NEDFi, DFS, MDoNER and state governments have worked together to identify financial gaps and develop state-specific interventions.
Between April and June 2026, the Secretary, MDoNER, held individual consultations with states, which subsequently set their own targets.
The Minister urged bankers to ensure that the Northeast's growing financial access translates into economic opportunities and that value generated in the region remains within the region.

title: Union Fisheries Secretary Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi Visits Mandapam Seaweed Cultivation Site; Interacts with Seaweed Farmers, Self-Help Groups and Scientists

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:

content:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India, visited the seaweed cultivation site at Munnaikadu, Mandapam Camp, Tamil Nadu, and interacted with seaweed farmers associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs). The visit was undertaken as part of the Department's efforts to promote seaweed farming, strengthen coastal livelihoods, and accelerate the development of the seaweed value chain in the country.
A day earlier, Dr. Likhi had chaired a meeting on seaweed farming at the ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre, Mandapam, Tamil Nadu, to review the progress of seaweed cultivation initiatives and discuss measures for scaling up production, value addition, and market linkages in the sector.
During the interaction, the farmers explained various cultivation techniques adopted in Tamil Nadu, including monoline and raft-based methods, and demonstrated different farming, maintenance and harvesting operations. The Secretary appreciated the contribution of women-led Self-Help Groups in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities through seaweed farming and encouraged the members to enhance production, bring more farmers into organized cultivation and avail benefits under Government schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY).
Earlier, the Union Secretary chaired a Meeting on Seaweed Farming at the ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre, Mandapam, with representatives from Coastal States and Union Territories, research institutions, technical agencies and seaweed stakeholders from across the country. He highlighted the significant potential of seaweed cultivation in India and noted that the country's coastline of
11,099 km
provides favourable conditions for large-scale expansion of the sector. Research institutions have identified
384 suitable sites
covering
24,707 hectares
for seaweed cultivation across Coastal States and Union Territories.
The Secretary informed that under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), seaweed cultivation has been identified as a priority activity for promoting employment generation and augmenting the incomes of fishers and coastal communities. During the period
2020-27, projects worth ₹181.11 crore
have been approved for seaweed development, including the establishment of a Seaweed Park in Tamil Nadu. Financial assistance has been extended for installation of
37,255 seaweed culture rafts and 44,080 seaweed culture monoline units
, along with support for seed banks, awareness, training and capacity-building initiatives.
The meeting was attended by Dr. Surabhi Rai, Joint Secretary (Marine Fisheries); Smt. Gunjan Krishna, Joint Secretary (Inland Fisheries), Department of Fisheries, Government of India; Dr. J. K. Jena, Deputy Director General (Fisheries Science), ICAR; Dr. Bijay Kumar Behera, Chief Executive, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB); and officials from the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, and State Fisheries Departments through hybrid mode.
Deliberations were held on key priorities for accelerating the growth of the seaweed sector, including the implementation of identified seaweed development action points, strengthening inter-agency coordination, establishing decentralized seed banks, addressing implementation challenges in projects supported under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), promoting entrepreneurship and market linkages, facilitating offshore seaweed cultivation, enhancing farmer outreach and capacity building, and expediting the operationalization of the Tamil Nadu Seaweed Park. Discussions also covered opportunities to expand the applications of seaweed in food, animal feed, fertilizers and other value-added products, as well as the formulation of a long-term roadmap for the sustainable and holistic development of the sector.
Background
Seaweed cultivation has emerged as a priority area under India's Blue Economy initiatives owing to its potential for livelihood generation, coastal community development and promotion of marine-based bio-economy activities. Seaweed production in India has increased from
18,890 tonnes in 2015 to 74,083 tonnes in 2024 and 82,728 tonnes in 2025.
The Department of Fisheries has adopted a cluster-based approach and
notified 34 fisheries production and processing clusters
across the country to strengthen value chains, improve competitiveness and enhance export potential. Under these initiatives
, Lakshadweep has been notified as a Seaweed Cluster
and the ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre, Mandapam has been designated as a Centre of Excellence for seaweed development and research. Institutional mechanisms in the form of an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) on Seaweed Development have also been established to facilitate coordinated sectoral development.

title: NLMC’s first end-to-end e-auction of RINL land parcels generates ₹366.33 Crore in successful bids on Day 1, 150 plots sold
subtitle:
Highest auction price crosses ₹1.80 lakh per square yard, reflecting strong market demand

Second Phase of RINL e-auction on October 30th
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 OCT 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, successfully conducted Day 1 of the e-auction of premium land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity operating Visakhapatnam Steel Plant. The first phase marks a significant milestone for NLMC, as it is the Corporation’s first end-to-end e-auction, demonstrating a structured, transparent and technology-driven approach towards monetising surplus public assets.
Of the land parcels offered in the first phase, 150 plots were successfully sold, generating a total successful bid value of ₹366.33 crore against an aggregate reserve price of ₹312.48 crore. The successful bids recorded an average premium of 17.23% over the reserve price, reflecting encouraging market participation and interest in the properties on offer.
The auction also recorded significant price realisation, with the highest auction price crossing ₹1.80 lakh per square yard. This strong price discovery reflects robust market demand for well-located land parcels in Visakhapatnam. It underscores the role of a transparent and competitive e-auction process in unlocking the economic potential of public assets.
The auction is being facilitated by NLMC in coordination with RINL, with Quikr India Private Limited (QIPL) serving as the Transaction Consultant. The online bidding process is being conducted through RailTel’s E-Nivida platform.
The e-auction forms part of the broader effort to facilitate the productive utilisation of surplus land assets held by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other government entities. Through a structured and market-driven process, NLMC works with asset-owning organisations to bring identified properties to the market, encourage participation from prospective buyers and support transparent value discovery.
Ahead of the auction, NLMC and RINL undertook investor outreach activities in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Hyderabad during September 2026. These meetings provided prospective bidders with an opportunity to understand the properties on offer, seek clarifications and familiarise themselves with the participation process.
The outreach programme also helped address queries relating to registration, documentation, Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) requirements and online bidding. These efforts were aimed at widening awareness, facilitating bidder participation and ensuring that interested buyers had access to relevant information before participating in the e-auction.
The successful outcome of Day 1 of the RINL land e-auction marks an important step in NLMC’s efforts to facilitate transparent and competitive monetisation of public assets. The response to the auction demonstrates the potential of well-structured market processes to attract investor interest and support value realisation from surplus government assets.
Final Opportunity to Own Land in Visakhapatnam: Second Phase of RINL E-Auction on October 30 -
Following the encouraging response to the first phase, the second and final phase of the e-auction offers prospective buyers another opportunity to acquire land parcels in key locations of Visakhapatnam. The second phase will cover the remaining 216 land parcels and has been rescheduled to October 30, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM. As this is the final phase of the current auction, interested buyers are encouraged to review the available plots and complete their registration within the prescribed timeline. The first-phase results provide prospective bidders with an indication of market participation and price discovery, making this an important opportunity for those looking to explore land ownership in Visakhapatnam.
Interested bidders must complete their registration by October 27, 2026. Details of the available land parcels, reserve prices, eligibility conditions and participation requirements can be accessed on the official e-auction portal:
https://eauction.enivida.com/
.
Prospective buyers are encouraged to review the available information, undertake due diligence and complete the necessary formalities before the deadline to participate in the final phase of the auction.
About NLMC
The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a Government of India company under the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. It facilitates the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other government agencies. NLMC works in coordination with asset-owning organisations to support the structured identification, preparation and monetisation of such assets through transparent and market-oriented processes.
